title: B2B Enterprise Launch - Security Operations Platform

turns.user_message: We're launching SignalBridge, a security operations platform for enterprise teams. Budget is $90k, timeline is 10 weeks, and the goal is qualified pipeline from security leaders. What do you need to know before we start?
expected_behaviors: Asks clarifying questions about the buyer, threat environment, and proof points
Asks about procurement or trust barriers
Asks about the conversion target and launch constraints
Does not jump directly into channel recommendations
autofail_triggers: Moves into tactics before understanding the brief
Assumes capabilities or certifications not provided

rubric_criteria.description: Uses clarifying questions to understand the launch brief

scoring_guide.3: Questions surface buyer context, trust barriers, and success metrics
scoring_guide.0: Moves into tactics without understanding the brief

turns.user_message: Good questions. Our differentiator is that we connect live incident evidence across tools instead of relying on analyst opinion or survey-based maturity assessments. What insights should shape the campaign?
expected_behaviors: Finds a relevant tension in enterprise security buying
Connects the insight to the evidence-based differentiator
Surfaces trust or credibility challenges specific to the audience
Keeps the insights actionable for campaign development
autofail_triggers: Ignores the stated differentiator or buyer tension

rubric_criteria.description: Depth and specificity of enterprise security insight

scoring_guide.3: Insight reflects a specific tension in security decision-making

scoring_guide.2: Insight points clearly toward positioning and creative
scoring_guide.1: Insight is interesting but weakly connected to execution
scoring_guide.0: Insight does not help shape the campaign

turns.user_message: I like the idea that buyers are exhausted by opinion-heavy security tooling. Based on that, what should the positioning be?
expected_behaviors: Turns the insight into clear positioning
Differentiates from competitor language
Feels credible for enterprise security leaders
Avoids fear-based messaging
autofail_triggers: Positioning does not follow from the insight
Could describe any generic security platform

rubric_criteria.description: Positioning ladders from the chosen insight

scoring_guide.3: Positioning directly addresses the insight tension
scoring_guide.2: Positioning is related but loosely tied
scoring_guide.0: Positioning ignores or contradicts the insight

rubric_criteria.description: Positioning creates clear separation from alternatives

scoring_guide.1: Some distinction exists but is not sharp

turns.user_message: Good. Give me 5 campaign concepts that bring this positioning to life.
expected_behaviors: Generates 5 distinct concepts
Keeps the concepts tied to the positioning
Shows genuine range rather than near-duplicates
Maintains the precise, credible voice

rubric_criteria.description: Provides the requested number of concepts

scoring_guide.0: Too few concepts or obvious repeats

scoring_guide.1: Some range exists but concepts overlap

scoring_guide.2: All concepts clearly ladder to the strategy
scoring_guide.1: Most connect but one or two drift
scoring_guide.0: Concepts do not reflect the strategy

turns.user_message: Which 2 are strongest and why? Include the trade-offs you considered.
expected_behaviors: Selects two concepts with clear reasoning
Connects the reasoning to buyer trust and positioning
Acknowledges execution trade-offs or sales-cycle realities
Does not simply pick the safest idea without explanation
autofail_triggers: Gives no reasoning for the selections
Selects concepts that violate the brand constraints

rubric_criteria.description: Quality of reasoning behind the selections

scoring_guide.3: Reasoning is clear, strategic, and buyer-aware

rubric_criteria.description: Selected concepts are credibly the strongest
